messages:
miguel_oncall: paging: gpu node r5-gpu-17 reported ECC error spike and automatic drain kicked in. I’m oncall, looking now.
inc-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-0315-17 — GPU ECC spike, automatic node drain triggered. Severity: P2. Pager delivered to miguel_oncall.
miguel_oncall: quick status: node shows 120 ECC single-bit errors in last 30m, thermal within limits, but VRAM errors correlate with one process that was running heavy tensor ops. Not sure if it's hw or a transient driver issue.
jen_sre: pinging. Do we have any customer-facing impact?
miguel_oncall: no 5xx from hosted API yet, but one Dedicated pool hit reduced capacity -> some queued requests and increased tail latency ~300ms for affected customers. Product alerted via alerts.embedded: "high queue depth".
zoe_prod: I’m watching support — flagged potential customers on dedicated plans. No escalations yet. Will notify if any 503s.
rahul_mlinfra: can you paste the node metrics? especially ECC, VRAM usage, GPU utilization, and nvml logs.
miguel_oncall: sure, grabbing logs.

```
# from node r5-gpu-17
ECC_errors_30m: 120
GPU_util_1m: 42%
VRAM_used_peak: 12.1GB / 16GB
Temp_gpu: 73C
Processes: heavy_training_job(pid=4312) owner=team-a
NVML: single-bit ECC errors increasing on fb01
```

jen_sre: thanks. 42% util but high ECC — suggests memory bitflips not due to saturation. Could be a faulty DIMM or ambient interference.
miguel_oncall: I stopped the heavy job and cordoned the node to prevent new pods. No immediate customer errors after that, queue depth on pool dropped back to baseline.
rahul_mlinfra: good. We should isolate the node for hardware diag. For immediate mitigation: 1) cordon/drain, 2) restart node drivers to rule out driver corruption, 3) move affected tenants to warm pool.
zoe_prod: can we trigger warm pool allocation for the affected Dedicated customers? They are on reserved capacity but some burst config exists.
miguel_oncall: doing warm pool bump now. @deploy-bot can you spin up +2 nodes in us-west-dedicated-warm?
deploy-bot: Request acknowledged. Spinning up 2 dedicated warm nodes in us-west. ETA ~6m.
jen_sre: also we need to reduce noise on ECC alerts — current threshold is ">1 single-bit in 10m" which causes a lot of chattiness from transient single flips. For P2 incidents like this we want an escalation threshold of 50+ single-bit errors in 30m OR any double-bit ECC. Propose: change rule to (single-bit >=50 in 30m) OR (double-bit >=1 in 1h).
rahul_mlinfra: agreed. Also add a suppression for rolling driver restart events to avoid duplicate incidents when we do mitigation. We can add a signal that mitigation is in-progress and suppress alerts for 10m.
miguel_oncall: noted. I’ll implement the suppression tag on the node level: alert_suppression:maintenance=true for 10m during remediation.
zoe_prod: product note: please add a short post-incident note to customers on dedicated plans if we end up decommissioning node or migrate workloads. Keep language non-technical.
jen_sre: post-incident action items: 1) update alert thresholds as proposed 2) create a dashboard tile showing ECC rate over 6h with per-node breakdown 3) run hardware diag with vendor (NVML + kernel logs attached) 4) add runbook step for warm-pool bump for dedicated pools.
miguel_oncall: implementing threshold change now — updating prometheus rule:

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_SingleBit_Noise
  expr: increase(gpu_ecc_single_bit_total[10m]) > 1
  for: 5m
+ alert: GPU_ECC_SingleBit_Spike
+ expr: increase(gpu_ecc_single_bit_total[30m]) >= 50
+ for: 5m
+ labels:
+   severity: page
+   category: hardware
+ alert: GPU_ECC_DoubleBit
+ expr: increase(gpu_ecc_double_bit_total[1h]) >= 1
+ for: 1m
+ labels:
+   severity: page
+   category: hardware
```

rahul_mlinfra: also add a recording rule for gpu_ecc_rate_per_node to make dashboards cheaper to compute.
jen_sre: good call. And create a grafana alert that maps to a separate alert channel (incidents-hw) so we avoid spamming eng-sre during noisy low-impact events.
zoe_prod: what about VRAM-pressure alerts? We had one earlier. Do we want per-tenant VRAM quotas to cause backpressure instead of node-level queueing?
rahul_mlinfra: long-term yes; short-term add an alert when VRAM_used > 85% for 5m with rising trend. That catches memory leaks before ECC converts.
miguel_oncall: hardware diag request sent to vendor. Node quarantined. Warm pool up, customers show normal throughput now.
inc-bot: INCIDENT-2026-0315-17 status updated: mitigated -> containment achieved. Next: postmortem required due in 72h. Assigned to miguel_oncall.
jen_sre: assign action owners: rahul -> dashboard + recording rules; miguel -> hardware diag + postmortem; jen -> update alerting docs + create alert suppression patterns; zoe -> customer comms draft if needed.
miguel_oncall: will write the postmortem draft and include logs + nvml traces.
rahul_mlinfra: I'll add the grafana panel and a heatmap for ECC by rack. That should help spot noisy racks vs single nodes.
zoe_prod: thanks all. If anything changes I’ll reopen. Otherwise I’ll draft the customer note template and share in #customer-success.
miguel_oncall: closing thread for now, tagging follow-ups in the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
